messages:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a weird regression on embeddings: mixed small (1-2 vectors) + huge (10k vectors) requests cause CPU spikes and a bunch of 413s from the gateway. Tried on canary.
Zoe: Ugh. Any reproducible curl or payload snippet?
Sam: Yep. Minimal repro (from devbox):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers: Authorization: Bearer $KEY, Content-Type: application/json
Body: { "input": [[0.1,...], ... 10000 vectors], "model": "rwd-embed-large" }
```
Response: 413 Payload Too Large OR 202 slow enqueue then timeout.
Mike: Are these single multi-array requests or batched multiple items? 413 suggests gateway limits, but the CPU spike smells like our splitter trying to plan an enormous subbatch.
Sam: Single request containing mixed sizes (payload assembled by a customer-side SDK). They expect split/route logic to chunk sequences but we end up doing expensive dim-detection across the whole body before routing.
Nina: That matches a perf trace I saw — preflight does a full-stream parse + dim inference step which is O(total_tokens) before we can short-circuit to route-by-size. We should be able to short-circuit on headers.
Zoe: We do have X-Embed-Estimate-Units header but it's opt-in and SDKs rarely set it. Can we default to a cheap estimate pass that samples the first N items and uses heuristics to pick a route quickly?
Mike: Sampling would help immediate routing, but quotas and billing need accurate units eventually. Idea: fast-path routing + deferred accurate accounting (post-acceptance audit). If audit fails, mark the request as charged differently and emit a telemetry flag.
Sam: That would preserve latency SLO for the common case. But customer-facing UX: failing later with an adjusted charge is bad. We need console signals and a clear rollout policy.
Nina: Console should show a new column: "estimated_units" vs "final_units" and a tiny badge if adjustment occurred. Also a flag in the response: `x-embed-routing-mode: sampled` or `exact`.
Zoe: Agreed. Also add a server-side softcap that converts oversized single-request payloads into a 202 with a status URL for async processing when estimate>threshold. Less surprising than charging adjustments.
Mike: Another angle: expand the sampling heuristic to detect extreme skew (one huge item + lots of small). If skew detected, prefer splitting the huge item off first and route small ones to fast-path. That should reduce latency tail for small ones.
Sam: Telemetry: we need a new histogram for "routing_decision_ms" and a boolean tag "sampling_used" plus outcome labels (ok, charged_adjusted, async_queued, rejected).
Nina: Also surface per-tenant quota impact: a tenant might get their small vectors fast but the huge one could exhaust their reserved capacity. Need quota simulation in console before applying fast-path.
Zoe: For rollout UX: feature flag `embed.routing.fast_sample_v1` default off; enable for internal tenants + canary, monitor telemetry for "final_units/estimated_units > 1.2" spike.
infra-bot: deploy started: embed-router:v2026-03-20-sample-fastpath -> canary (3 pods).
Mike: I'll wire the telemetry and the response header today. Nina can do console column and quota sim. Zoe can update SDK to set X-Embed-Estimate-Units when possible. Sam will run load to validate.
Sam: Plan sounds good. Quick follow-ups: 1) choose sampling N (I'm leaning N=16), 2) threshold for async queue (maybe 5M tokens), 3) exact header name for badge.
Nina: N=16 OK. Async threshold set to 5_000_000 tokens for now. Header: `X-Embed-Routing-Mode`.
Zoe: SDK PR incoming, will set estimate header when user passes an array of arrays or an explicit vector-count hint.
Mike: I'll add the metrics and the guardrail alarms. Sam — ping when you have the load run so we can flip the flag in canary. :thumbsup:
Sam: Will do, thanks all.
